mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk appetite and compressed credit spreads.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 5.5% predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as higher unemployment expectations suppress equity risk premiums.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) when UNRATE > 5.5% in the current month.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (household spending index) above 1020 predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as stronger consumer demand supports corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in 70% of months when HOUST > 1020 (rolling 12-month IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 2% over three months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak manufacturing momentum reduces growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months by ≥2%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO declines ≥2% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and UNRATE both rise simultaneously by more than 0.2 percentage points in the prior month, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to heightened policy uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS up >0.2pp AND UNRATE up >0.2pp in the prior month
regime_hint: Dual tightening in monetary policy and labor market
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of such joint moves (rolling IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (employment months) below 138,000 in a month triggers a positive S&P 20-day forward return as labor market weakness can precede a rebound in investor sentiment.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls below 138,000 in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS < 138,000 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL (CPI) increase above 0.3% followed by a subsequent month of no change is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as the market anticipates inflation stabilization.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises >0.3% in month t and remains flat in month t+1
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive when CPIAUCSL meets this pattern (rolling IC < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP demand) grows at a quarterly rate exceeding 4% in the prior quarter, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to excessive economic momentum and possible overvaluation.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth >4% in prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when GDPC1 grows >4% quarterly (t-test p < 0.05).
